messages:
carla: Heads-up — saw a small burst of Xid errors on 3 cards in us-east-2 over the last 10m. Prom alert fired twice but nodes stayed healthy. Suspect exporter chattiness rather than card death. Posting DCGM snippet + Prom query we used.

mike: Can you paste the raw PromQL you used?

carla: Sure — ran this to group by card_id + driver_bucket:
```
sum by(node, card_id, driver_bucket) (increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[5m]))
```
Result: three cards had a 1->2 spike but none had ECC increments.

priyanka: If ECC stayed 0 that suggests transient PCI hiccups or driver noise. We should suppress single-sample Xid alerts unless they meet a quorum: either >2 distinct Xids within 5m for same card OR an ECC increment within 10m.

leon: I like the quorum idea. Also let's bucket by driver version — older drivers show more single-shot Xids in our history. We should avoid masking real fails from wearout.

mike: Proposal for a Prom rule (pseudocode):
```
# alert only if 3+ xid increments in 5m OR any xid + ecc increase in 10m
alert: GPU_Xid_Unhealthy
expr: (
  sum by(node, card_id) (increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[5m])) >= 3
) or (
  increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[5m]) >= 1 and increase(dcgm_memory_ecc_errors_total[10m]) > 0
)
for: 2m
labels:
  severity: page
```
We'll also add `driver_bucket` and `mig_instance` as labels to help triage.

dcgm-bot: Reminder — exporter 0.8.3 includes a noise-filtering flag `--xid-debounce-ms`. We currently run 0.8.1 in us-east-2.

carla: Good catch — that explains part of it. Upgrading exporter would reduce noise. But rolling that everywhere will take time; let's patch Prom rules first.

priyanka: Can we also add a recording rule to capture a 1h streak metric so we can see repeated low-rate failures (wearout)? e.g., `gpu_xid_streak{node,card_id}=increase(dcgm_xid_errors_total[1h])` and alert if that grows over 24h beyond a threshold.

leon: Also we should correlate with GPU temperature and PCI resets. Add these to the alert context so oncall has quick links: temp history, driver version, last pci_reset.

mike: I'll open a PR with the rule + recording rule + dashboard panel. Will include a test job that replays the sample we saw to verify suppression.

carla: For runbook: if alert fires after new rule, consider: 1) check ECC counts, 2) ssh and `nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,DRIVER`, 3) check k8s pods on node — if noisy but healthy, bump to monitor. If ECC > 0 or repeated xid streak, plan drain + replace.

carla: runbook snippet:
```
# quick triage
kubectl get nodes -l gpu=true -o wide
kubectl describe node $NODE | grep -i pci
ssh $NODE 'nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,DRIVER,ATOMS'
# if sustained xid > 5 in 24h or any ECC > 0 => cordon+drain and GPU RMA flow
```

oncall: tagging @oncall — we'll watch the suppression PR for 24h after deploy. Please include a simple grafana panel showing raw xid + recording rule so we can flip the rule quickly if we miss a real failure.

priyanka: Agree. Also scheduled a canary roll of exporter 0.8.3 in us-east-2a tomorrow to see if noise drops.

mike: PR: https://git.redwood/infrastructure/ops/+/1234 — contains prom rules, recording rule, test job, and dashboard draft.

carla: Thanks — will monitor and report back after canary + rule deploy. :thumbsup:
